issues: Whether the passport program's duty of procedural fairness required disclosure of the full investigative record (facial recognition comparison results, police and investigator emails, internal investigation report, references to uncharged/other criminal allegations) before revoking the passport
Whether providing only a 'summary' of findings, rather than the underlying material relied upon, satisfies the duty to disclose the case to meet
Whether reliance on undisclosed facial recognition comparison evidence to find identity misrepresentation breaches procedural fairness
Whether referencing other criminal charges never put to the affected person in the fairness letters violates the right to know and respond to the case against him
What remedy follows a breach of procedural fairness in this context — whether the revocation decision and the refusal-of-services period must be quashed or remitted for redetermination
Whether the decision-maker's conclusion that the response 'did not neutralize the findings' was reasonable given the undisclosed material
What level/content of procedural fairness applies to passport revocation and denial-of-service decisions
Whether the Canadian Passport Order and related policy create a right to disclosure of the investigative file prior to decision
key_facts: Client held and had renewed a Canadian passport under a name used for years without prior issue
A provincial ID office flagged him, triggering a federal passport investigation
Passport Program sent fairness letters alleging false/misleading information and use of an assumed identity, and noting an indictable charge for breach of release condition
Client responded with a court order for delayed birth registration, resulting birth registration, and a sworn declaration in his current name
A second letter stated the response did not neutralize the findings
Director revoked the passport and imposed approximately a five-year refusal of passport services

On judicial review, the certified/produced record revealed material never disclosed to him: facial recognition comparison results (matching current-name photos but not earlier-name passports), police/provincial investigator emails, an incomplete internal investigation report, and references to other criminal charges never raised in the fairness letters
causes_of_action: Application for judicial review of administrative decision (passport revocation and refusal of services) on grounds of breach of procedural fairness
Alternatively, unreasonableness of the decision under Vavilov standard
candidate_statutes: Department of Foreign Affairs, Trade and Development Act
Canadian Charter of Rights and Freedoms (mobility rights, s.6; s.7 possibly engaged)
